newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission sets method for calculating penalties.
newsitem.headline: Commission sets method for calculating penalties.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday agreed on a method for calculating financial penalties which can and no doubt will be imposed on member states who ignore Court of Justice rulings.

Although the Commission merely decided on the method and did not discuss specific cases EU officials said the new system -- foreseen under article 171 of the Maastricht Treaty -- could be used in five cases in early 1997.
The Commission last year agreed on the criteria which should be applied for the sanctions, pointing to factors such as seriousness, duration and damage.
What it lacked was a mathematical formula for calculating the sanctions.

What it decided on Wednesday was to set a basic fine of 500 Ecus per day, which would be varied on the basis of two coefficients -- one (from one to 20) concerning seriousness and the other (from one to three) on duration.

To give the fines a dissuasive effect the Commission has also built in a factor relating the fine to a country's gross domestic product and its number of votes to take into account the weight it had in deciding on the legislation in question.

EU officials said the new system could be used within one month in three cases where Germany has ignored court rulings on ground water, surface water and bird protection and two cases where Italy has ignored legislation on waste disposal in Campania.
These would go to the Court, which will take a final decision on the fine. The Court could take up to a year to take its decision, EU officials said.
